tools.name: carrier_attach-subscriber-host
tools.description: Attaches (or re-links) the subscriber's gateway host. A subscriber has at most one host; supplying a DIFFERENT host replaces the current one in place (RMA re-link). **Not idempotent.** Re-sending the host this subscriber is already linked to is rejected with `409 gateway_already_attached` — nothing is written. A host linked to a *different* subscriber in the organization is `409 gateway_already_linked`. Read `GET /subscribers/{id}` (field `hostId`) if you need to know the current link before calling; `prevHostId` on a successful response is the host that was replaced (`null` on a fresh attach). Because a repeat is an error rather than a no-op, do NOT blindly retry a request that timed out — re-read the subscriber first, or treat `409 gateway_already_attached` as 'already applied'. Requires scope `update:subscribers`. Required: id, hostId. Returns the updated HostLinkResponse.

Optional: email, metadata, name (plus 3 more).

params.name: limit
params.description: Page size — how many subscribers to return per page. Alias: pageSize. Must be an integer from 1 to 500. Anything else is rejected with 400 validation_failed naming whichever of the two spellings you sent and the bound it broke: a non-numeric value (abc, 1.5), a value below 1 (0, -1), or a value above 500. Nothing is silently rounded or clamped — if you ask for 1000 you get an error stating the maximum is 500, not a page of 500. Omit the parameter for the default of 50.

params.description: Absent leaves it unchanged; JSON null clears it. The 255 limit is bytes of UTF-8.

tools.name: protect_pos-transaction
tools.description: Records a point of sale transaction as a camera event so the transaction details can be overlaid on recorded footage. Requires write access to the target camera. Footage capture is best-effort: the overlay only appears where the target camera was recording the transaction window (e.g. cameras in detections or adaptive recording modes), and a backdated timestamp may fall outside retained footage. A 200 response confirms the event was recorded, not that video exists for the window. Required: id, amount, externalId, type. Optional: currency, lineItems, location (plus 2 more). Returns the new PosTransactionResponse.

params.name: currency
params.description: Uppercase ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. USD

params.name: externalId
params.description: Caller-supplied transaction id, unique per camera. Used for best-effort idempotency within a short window (in-memory, per-process; it resets on restart, so a retry after a restart or after the window elapses may create a duplicate event).

params.name: timestamp
params.description: Transaction time in epoch milliseconds. Must be within the last 24 hours and no more than 5 minutes ahead of server time; out-of-range values are rejected. A value within the allowed skew is clamped to now.

novel_features.name: Path and capability probe
novel_features.description: See which transports and products answer on each console. Write status is yes, no or unproven, and a probe alone never reports yes.

novel_features.name: Impact and lockout check
novel_features.description: Estimate from the last sync what a proposed action would take down and whether it risks your way back in. It never reports safe.

novel_features.name: Journaled change with undo
novel_features.description: Send one change to an official Network or Protect path with a journaled before-image, a read-back check and undo. Nothing is sent without --confirm.

novel_features.name: Config drift
novel_features.description: See field-level config changes between two synced snapshots, marked attributed (in the change journal) or out-of-band.

novel_features.name: What happened since I looked
novel_features.description: One timeline, built from local syncs, of state changes, ISP dips, drift, newcomers and journaled changes.

novel_features.name: Newcomer detection
novel_features.description: List clients, devices and cameras first seen at a sync in a window.

novel_features.name: Firewall rule prediction
novel_features.description: Predict which firewall policy would match a hypothetical packet. This is a local prediction with no API confirmation.

novel_features.name: Device topology tree
novel_features.description: See gateway, switches and APs as a tree per console, from the last sync.
